newsitem.title: USA: March U.S. industry output seen boosting Q1 growth.
newsitem.headline: March U.S. industry output seen boosting Q1 growth.

text.p: Strong gains in U.S. industrial output in March show the economy grew more swiftly than previously thought in the first quarter and may suggest inflation pressures are on the rise, analysts said.
The Federal Reserve reported industrial production up 0.9 percent last month, higher than the consensus forecast for a 0.6 percent increase. Output rose 0.6 percent in February.
In addition, capacity utilization surged to a two-year high of 84.1 percent from 83.6 percent the month before.
But capacity itself may be growing fast enough to accommodate growing demand, and that should lead to lower utilization rates eventually, some analysts said.
Capacity growth in March stood at about a 4.0-percent annual rate, meaning industrial output could expand at a 4.0-percent rate without further straining capacity.
Still, production would have to slow significantly from its March rate in order to ease any resource strains.
"Industrial production cannot grow at a 10-percent annual rate ... without capacity utilization increasing," said Peter Kretzmer, senior economist at NationsBanc Capital Markets Inc.

Looking ahead, analysts projected slower demand growth in the second quarter. But they said industrial output was likely to record robust monthly gains in the near term, gains that could bring upticks to the capacity use rate and add to inflation fears.
"I think we're going to slow down in spending here, but when we slow down in production, we're going to still be at a pace that builds capacity utilization," said Sanwa's Strauss.
Despite the strong March showing, however, the industrial production data offer little insight into the course of monetary policy, Strauss said.
"(Central bankers') whole issue is not current inflation, it's the risk for inflation next year," he said.
